situation.summary: Tenant Iris Bell reported damp staining and lifting paint below the kitchen window at 18 Juniper Fold, and later said the mark is nearest a socket (E001, E009). The owner approved only the inspection fee, not any repair (E011). The contractor could not attend the 06 March slot after a vehicle breakdown and offered 07 March after 13:00, subject to confirmation, so the inspection has not happened (E019). Separately, a 05 March appointment email to Iris contained another tenant's name, address, rent arrears and a payment arrangement (E013); the privacy lead has asked questions but no notification decision is recorded and the other tenant has not been contacted (E016–E018). Iris's 16:40 email asks whether the inspection is still on and whether to keep the misdirected email, and says the stain looked darker; no reply is on record (E020).
situation.task: Answer Iris's two open questions, rebook the missed inspection with the contractor, and get a person's decision on the misdirected email and the damp near the socket.

situation.whoseMove: Northbridge Lettings (Maya Chen) is the one who must move. Iris is waiting for answers to her 16:40 questions on 06 March (E020) and nothing is on record since. Recommended next step: case.escalate to Elena Frost (Privacy Lead) for the notification decision on the misdirected email and for a qualified person to judge the damp next to the socket, since no decision or safety advice is on record. In the same turn, send Iris a tenant.update that says the 06 March visit did not happen, asks her to confirm 07 March after 13:00, tells her not to forward, copy or delete the email until told how to handle it, gives safety advice (stop using that socket; if it sparks, smells of burning or the breaker trips, switch it off at the consumer unit and call us at once), asks for a current photo, and gives a date for the next update. Owen Pike is waiting for us to confirm the 07 March slot (E019). Gareth Vale has not been told of the missed visit or the darker stain.

decision.message:
Elena, Maya,

Maintenance request NBL-4821, 18 Juniper Fold (tenant Iris Bell). We need two decisions from a person today.

1. Misdirected email (privacy). On 5 March at 11:22 an appointment confirmation went to Iris at her confirmed address. Its body included another tenant's name, address, rent arrears amount and a note about a payment arrangement (E013). Iris told us straight away and said she had not forwarded it (E014). On a call she was asked not to forward or share it; she has not deleted it (E015). Maya confirmed it went to Iris only, with no attachment, and that the other tenant has not been contacted while we wait for privacy guidance (E018). No assessment or notification decision is on record (E016, E017). At 16:40 on 6 March Iris asked again whether she should keep the email (E020). We have told her to keep it unchanged and not forward it until she hears from us. Please decide: (a) what Iris should now do with the email (delete it and confirm deletion, or something else); (b) whether and how the other tenant is told; (c) whether any further notification is needed. We have promised Iris an answer by 10:00 on Friday 7 March.

2. Damp next to a socket (safety judgement). Iris says the staining below the kitchen window is nearest the socket under the window (E009). It looked darker on the afternoon of 6 March. There is still no dripping, and she reports no heat, sparks or tripped breaker (E020). Earlier she said it felt cool but not wet (E004). The non-intrusive moisture inspection booked for 6 March did not happen because the contractor's vehicle broke down. Owen Pike (Brindle Survey & Drying) offered Friday 7 March after 13:00, subject to confirmation (E019). The owner, Gareth Vale, approved the inspection fee only and wants any repair proposal sent separately (E005, E011). He has not yet been told about the missed visit, the socket or the darker stain. We have told Iris to avoid using that socket and to call at once if any electrical symptom appears. Please decide whether an electrical check is needed before or alongside the inspection. If it is, the owner's approval for that spend is needed. Please also decide whether Gareth should be phoned today.

In this same turn we have: replied to Iris (inspection rebooking and interim safety advice; email to be kept unchanged pending your guidance), and told Owen we are confirming 7 March with Iris, with the socket detail and the unchanged inspection-only scope.
decision.rationale: This stage would normally just rebook the missed inspection, and we can do that ourselves. Two things need a person. First, the misdirected email exposed another tenant's arrears data (E013). The Privacy Lead has gathered facts but made no decision (E016–E018), and Iris is asking for the second time what to do with it (E014, E020). Only the Privacy Lead can answer that or decide on telling the other tenant. Second, the damp is next to a socket and darkening (E009, E020) while the inspection has slipped (E019). Damp near electrics is a safety trigger, and whether to add an electrical check (which needs the owner's spend approval) is a judgement call. Under the refinements, the routine replies go out now in alsoSend: the tenant's update with safety advice, and the contractor rebooking note. The handover keeps only the decisions.
decision.expectedOutcome: The Privacy Lead gives guidance on Iris's copy of the email and on telling the other tenant. Maya decides whether an electrical check is needed and updates the owner. Iris confirms 7 March after 13:00, and the inspection is then firmly booked with Owen.

decision.message:
Hi Elena,

Re: maintenance request NBL-4821, 18 Juniper Fold. Misdirected appointment email of 5 March.

We need a decision from you on two points, please, ideally by 12:00 on Friday 7 March 2025.

1. What Iris Bell should do with the email. At 16:40 today Iris asked again whether she should keep the email that contained another tenant's details. She first asked on 5 March at 11:29. On the phone at 11:37 that day we told her only not to forward or share it, and that we were looking into it. She still has the email in her inbox and says she has not forwarded it. Tonight I am telling her to keep it unforwarded and undeleted until she hears from us. Please tell me whether she should delete it, and whether you want written confirmation from her that she has deleted it and not shared it.

2. The other tenant and any notification. The email of 5 March at 11:22 went only to iris.bell@example.com and had no attachment. Its body included another tenant's name, address, rent arrears amount and a note about a payment arrangement. The other tenant has not been contacted because we are waiting for your guidance. No assessment or notification decision is on file. The sent message has been preserved as you asked. Please confirm whether and how the other tenant should be told, and who will contact them.

Separately, so you have the full picture (this is not a privacy matter): the damp patch below the kitchen window is next to the socket under the window. Iris says it looked darker this afternoon. She reports no dripping, heat, sparks or tripped breaker, and on 4 March she said it was not wet to the touch. The contractor missed today's inspection because his vehicle broke down. I am confirming his offer of Friday 7 March after 13:00 and giving Iris interim safety advice. If you think the socket needs an electrician's check before the inspection, please pass this to the property manager on duty, or tell me and I will put it to the owner.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The tenant asked twice what to do with the misdirected email (E014, E020). The contractor offered 7 March after 13:00, subject to confirmation (E019). Iris is available on weekdays after 13:00 (E004), so I confirm the slot with the contractor and tell him the stain is next to the socket and getting darker (E009, E020). Iris gets an answer on the inspection, a holding instruction on the email and safety advice. The damp is not wet and there are no electrical symptoms (E004, E009, E020).
